target_customer: Website owners and product teams who want fast, relevant search on their sites and apps without running search servers
problem: Site search was either weak built in tools or complex enterprise systems requiring servers and setup; Swiftype offered an API delivered search that could be added in minutes.
business_model: SaaS subscription tiered by usage, later enterprise search
product_category: Hosted site and app search API

founders.name: Matt Riley
founders.background_notes: Early engineer at Scribd; later a YC visiting partner per YC page.

founders.name: Quin Hoxie
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as a former tech lead for Elasticsearch.

competitors.name: Google
competitors.what: Site search via Google Custom Search

competitors.name: Endeca
competitors.what: Enterprise search requiring servers and complex setup

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a crawler, indexing and a relevance layer on Elasticsearch was a bet on then new technology but standard engineering; one founder came from Elasticsearch.

defensibility.rationale: Developer experience and indexed content created mild lock in, but search APIs could be rebuilt on the same open source engine.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google Custom Search remained a free alternative; Elastic, whose engine Swiftype was built on, bought it in November 2017.

market_need_then: In 2013 Swiftype reported over 70,000 sites and 130 million queries per month, growing to about 200 million queries per month by September 2013, showing strong demand for easy site search.

branding.domain_note: Used swiftype.com; acquisition details not found.

identity.logo: retired after the Elastic acquisition when products were regrouped under the Elastic brand

rebrands.to: Elastic Site Search and Elastic App Search
rebrands.why: Products folded into Elastic brand hierarchy after the acquisition.

branding.community_and_virality: Active blog and early adopter of Elasticsearch with ties to its community; no merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known to developers and YC alumni with 70,000 plus sites at its 2013 peak, though the brand was retired after acquisition.

pivots.why: YC page describes products across site, app and enterprise search; Elastic planned enterprise search expansion at acquisition.

outcome_analysis: Swiftype turned site search into an API developers could add in minutes, raised 1.7 million seed in August 2013 from a16z, NEA and Kleiner, a 7.5 million Series A from NEA a month later and a reported 13 million in 2015, and grew to hundreds of millions of monthly queries. Elastic acquired it in November 2017 for an undisclosed price and folded the products into its enterprise search offering.
notes: Series B 13M in March 2015 is from Dealroom plus a TechCrunch headline cited via search summary (Swiftype Raises 13M More); the article body was not read. Competitors come from 2013 TechCrunch coverage, after the W12 batch. Funding dates before 2013 (YC deal, earlier angels) not found. Wikipedia fetch was redirected and not retried.
